The Ides of March
THE SCENE: March 15, 44 B.C. A meeting
hall adjacent to Pompey's theater.
THE ACT: Surrounded by 60 "honorable"
men he had previously pardoned, Caesar
is stabbed 23 times.
THE IMMEDIATE AFTERMATH: Brutus
turns to deliver a speech on republican
liberty. The Senate, terrified, simply
stampedes out of the hall. The assassins
march through the streets expecting
cheers from the masses. Instead, they
are met with the furious, grieving riots
of the Roman proletariat.
THE REALITY: The people knew exactly
what had happened. They had lost their
champion to a cartel of landlords.
